comments.author: AnotherGoodName
comments.why: Slow-motion recording shows keyboard not typing the tapped letter.
comments.text: Fwiw it becomes really really obvious when companies have someone at the top pushing for initiatives like this and when they don't. A great example is how Apple used to be great at this. These days.the.keyboard.is.practically.unusable. As in it still doesn't type out the letter you tapped and you can see this via slow motion video recording [VIDEO] It's not at all wrong to call out subordinates in the company for quality feel. It may seem like it leads to misprioritization (everyone in the company scrambles to fix the issue you saw) but not doing this at all is far far worse. Look at this issue BillG raised and the fact that no one cared until it was raised. Big companies are very siloed by nature. The only thing that breaks these silos is the leadership doing things like this.

comments.author: ramity
comments.story: iPhone Typos? It's Not Just You – The iOS Keyboard Is Broken [video]
comments.why: Shows slide to type enabled at a given timestamp.
comments.text: 35m ago edit: Apple uses many predictive systems for typing. My sentiment in pointing out just slide to type might be misguided as it does not exist in a vacuum. I'd love to see these tests redone with slide to type disabled. I'm leaving the original comment below for reference. Slide to type. This "issue" is at most 6 years old for iOS users. Turn off slide to type if you do not use it. Slide to type does key resizing logic. This is the direct cause of this issue. Please upvote this comment for visibility. Please reply if you think I'm wrong. I see this get posted frequently enough I'm actually losing it. Please refer to [VIDEO] (timestamp 1:12) to see that slide to type is enabled.

comments.author: ProfessorLayton
comments.story: Report: Tim Cook could step down as Apple CEO 'as soon as next year'
comments.text: It’s not a silly comment, both macOS and iOS have been decaying into dog shit over the years from obvious bugs that anyone who uses the apps and features being sold would run into very quickly. Tim and other executives might be using their devices as email machines, but it’s not obvious they’re using everything they’re quite literally selling us. A few random examples: 1: The iOS keyboard is literally broken [VIDEO] 2: The Music app is barely functional, and will regularly fail to play music. Here it is bugging out, and stacking multiple album covers [LINK] 3: Offloading an app does not actually save any space [LINK] There’s so many more, and none of these examples are edge cases.
